title: The safety scan with the prompts off
outcomes: Runs both scan questions without a prompt in mixed positions
Answers a real threat with a move that stops it
Spends the move on a plan when the last move threatened nothing
Tells a real attack from an attack on a defended piece

steps.text: In "The safety scan: look before you move" and "Before every move: two questions" the questions were put to you. Now they are not. In mixed positions, some with a threat and some without, ask them yourself. **Ignore a real threat** and you lose material. **Answer a threat that is not there** and you lose a move. Both mistakes cost.

steps.caption: White to move. The rook on d8 faces the knight on d4. Is that a threat?

line.say: The pawn on e3 defends the knight on d4. The knight on c5 is loose, so the rook takes it.
...the pawn takes back. Black gave a rook for a knight, on top of the knight lost on c5.

claims.statement: The knight on c5 is the only loose Black piece.
Rxc5 wins at least a knight along the engine line.

steps.text: **The question behind both mistakes:** after a quiet move from me, can the opponent win material or mate? Check loose pieces and mate threats first. An attack on a piece that is defended is a threat only if the attacker is worth *less* than the target (a rule of thumb; count to be sure). When there is no threat, spend the move on your plan.

steps.title: Same attack, one change
steps.prompt: Black's rook faces the knight. Decide whether White must react. Predict, then check.
In your next game, mark two moves: one where you found a threat and one where you decided there was none. Write both on paper. What did each cost you in time?
